entry.summary: CAPE-JEPA - Cross-modal Adversarial Probabilistic Embedding JEPA arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses cross-modal remote sensing image retrieval, where images from different sensors such as SAR and multispectral imagery must be matched. It proposes CAPE-JEPA, which uses a probabilistic predictor that outputs a mean and variance per image patch, an adversarial regularizer that aligns modality distributions, and contrastive learning for scene-level discrimination. On the BigEarthNet-14K and fMoW datasets, it outperforms X-JEPA and other baselines while using fewer parameters (407.30M versus 432.72M).

entry.title: Rubric Curriculum RL: Training AI on Open-Ended Tasks by Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap
entry.summary: Rubric Curriculum RL: Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap in Non-Verifiable Domains arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces Rubric Curriculum RL (RcRL), a reinforcement learning method for open-ended tasks where answers cannot be automatically verified. It combines pairwise comparisons of model outputs with a curriculum over rubric criteria, requiring no new data, human annotations, or stronger teacher models. The authors report a 70.5% human win rate over the base model on creative writing and gains of 14.6% (full set) and 25.4% (consensus subset) on HealthBench. They also state that RcRL keeps improving beyond 1000 training steps, while baselines plateau within a few hundred.

entry.title: Topological Features for Segmenting X-Ray Hyperspectral Images
entry.summary: Homology Features for X-Ray Hyperspectral Images Segmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the difficulty of classifying multi-energy X-ray transmission hyperspectral images, which have high-dimensional redundancy and nonlinear spectral overlap. The authors compute Vietoris-Rips persistent homology on UMAP-projected superpixel point clouds to capture H1 cyclic structures that reflect spectral heterogeneity. These topological features are merged with pixel-level CNN features through a broadcasting mechanism. Experiments show the hybrid model outperforms CNN-only and superpixel-pooling baselines, indicating topology adds complementary information.

entry.title: Do Agents Need to Sleep? Borrowing Sleep Theory to Manage Persistent Memory
entry.summary: Do agents need to sleep? arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper argues that LLM-based agents that run across sessions and accumulate memory through interaction show problems such as semantic drift, weaker retrieval precision, propagation of stored errors, and memory saturation. It maps the three phases of the selectionist "ringing, resonance and renormalization" (RRR) account of sleep onto operations feasible in digital memory architectures. The authors predict that selectionist consolidation will outperform instructionist alternatives as memory stores grow large.

entry.title: Consistent submodular maximization when the full future is known
entry.summary: Consistent Submodular Maximization with Full Foresight arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies online submodular maximization under a limited recourse budget, where an algorithm keeps at most k arrived elements and makes a constant number of changes per step. Assuming the entire future is known and computation is unlimited, it identifies optimal approximation thresholds of 3/4 for deterministic algorithms and about 0.7942 for randomized ones. For any ε>0, the worst-case recourse is polynomial in 1/ε, independent of k and stream length. Matching impossibility results are proven even for coverage functions.

entry.title: FedXCrop: privacy-preserving federated learning for detecting crop diseases, with explanations of the aggregated model under uneven farm data
entry.summary: FedXCrop: Privacy-Preserving Crop Disease Detection via Federated Learning with Post-Aggregation Explainability under Non-IID Farm Distributions arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents FedXCrop, a federated learning pipeline that classifies crop diseases from leaf images without farms sharing raw data. It compares centralized training with federated training (FedAvg and FedProx) under varying label skew across clients. The authors also quantitatively evaluate Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad explanations of the aggregated global model.

entry.title: A Formal Definition of Catastrophic AI Performance
entry.summary: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the problem of AI objectives failing to match human preferences and introduces a formal definition of catastrophic performance. The definition relies on two reference values: a baseline value obtained if no agent is deployed, and an orthogonal value for trajectories unrelated to human preferences, which is typically far worse than the baseline. The authors illustrate the concept with examples in which an AI agent undoes benefits previously created by human activity.

entry.title: Generative image communication over underwater acoustic channels using cross-modal semantic refinement
entry.summary: Cross-Modal Semantic Successive Refinement for Generative Image Communication over Underwater Acoustic Channels arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a framework for transmitting images over underwater acoustic channels, which have limited bandwidth and complex conditions. The transmitter sends text descriptions, compact bottleneck features, and residual-vector-quantized visual side information, and the receiver fuses text and bottleneck features before refining and reconstructing the image with a one-step Pixel Mean Flow model. Simulations using COCO 2017 images and measured Watermark channel records show that layered unequal error protection helps recovery at low SNRs.

entry.title: CoSafe: Cooperative Safety Assurance for Self-Driving Cars in Mixed Traffic
entry.summary: CoSafe: Cooperative Runtime Safety Assurance for Mixed-Traffic Autonomous Driving arXiv · Nov 4, 2026CoSafe is a cooperative runtime safety framework for autonomous driving in mixed traffic, where self-driving cars share roads with human drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians. It uses vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication so roadside units can monitor scene-level hazards and jointly mitigate those involving multiple vehicles. Integrated with seven state-of-the-art autonomous driving systems and tested on the InterDrive benchmark, it reportedly raised driving scores by 70.03% on average and reduced safety violations by 87.80%. It also achieved an F3 score of 0.930 in identifying unsafe autonomous vehicles while meeting real-time constraints.

entry.title: BiCG-Net: A method for judging image quality of a specific object region rather than the whole picture
entry.summary: BiCG-Net: Target-Specific Image Quality Assessment via Observation Modeling and In-Image Differencing arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper estimates the quality of a specific target region, such as a train body, instead of the whole image. It samples patches expanding outward from the target box and infers quality from their relative structure. A compact student network, BiCG-Net, distills an 11-teacher ensemble through a linear observation model and in-image differencing. On CSIQ and LIVEC, the student reaches PLCCs of 0.9009 and 0.9133 against human MOS.

entry.title: Object detection without human labels, using collaborating foundation models
entry.summary: Annotator-Free Object Detection via Foundation Model Collaboration arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes an object detection framework that needs no human annotations on the target dataset. It combines the complementary strengths of pretrained foundation models, such as segmentation and vision-language systems, within a self-refining training loop that iteratively improves localization and classification. A landmark-based clustering mechanism shares labeling across image clusters to reduce costly queries to large vision-language models. Reported results on COCO, LVIS, ODinW-35, and Roboflow-100 show gains over prior open-vocabulary and long-tail methods, reaching 60.8 AP on COCO and 47.4 AP on LVIS in zero-shot settings.

entry.title: Cross-asset knowledge transfer for early fault detection on data-scarce assets without target fault data
entry.summary: Cross-Asset Knowledge Transfer for Early Fault Detection of Data-Scarce Assets Without Target Fault Data arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses early fault detection for industrial assets where the target asset has only normal-condition data and no fault samples, transferring diagnostic knowledge from a data-rich source asset. It proposes a zero-shot domain adaptation framework that labels source run-to-failure data with an exponentially weighted moving average chart, uses an Adapted Domain-Adversarial Neural Network with a Maximum Mean Discrepancy penalty, and applies ahead-of-time labeling for incipient faults. On a public bearing run-to-failure dataset, the method achieves the highest mean F1-score among four transfer baselines and its robustness is tested under synthetic noise.

entry.title: GPUMAP: GPU-Accelerated Progressive Dimensionality Reduction for Interactive Analysis
entry.summary: GPUMAP: GPU-Accelerated Progressive Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents GPUMAP, a progressive dimensionality reduction algorithm built on UMAP and accelerated with GPU parallelism for interactive use. The authors restructure UMAP's operations into a progressive pipeline and add modifications such as operation queues, instance-wise local join, and scheduling strategies. The implementation enables interactive analysis of million-scale datasets on commodity GPUs. The paper also studies how progressive projections evolve over time relative to the ground truth and how biased data streams affect projection quality and stability.

entry.title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
entry.summary: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes GEdit, a framework for updating knowledge in large language models that accounts for the geometric structure of their internal representations. It uses a Low-Rank Plus Diagonal factor model to capture the low-rank structure of Transformer feed-forward hidden representations, protecting a core knowledge subspace and adjusting regularization strength per edit. Experiments on GPT2-XL, GPT-J, and LLaMA-3-8B, with up to 10,000 continuous updates, report that GEdit outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in editing success and knowledge preservation.

entry.title: Rohbau3D-Semantics: A dataset of labeled laser scans of building shell construction sites
entry.summary: Rohbau3D-Semantics: Dense Semantic and Instance Labels for Point Clouds of Indoor Shell Construction Scenes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper releases Rohbau3D-Semantics, a dataset that adds dense semantic and instance labels to laser scan point clouds of shell construction sites. It contains 504 scenes from 14 survey sites, captured with a terrestrial laser scanner and preserving real scanning artifacts and non-uniform sampling. The labels cover 17 building component classes plus one background class, and scripts are provided to derive panoramic and cube-map representations.

entry.title: Chiron: LLM-Driven Cache Management for AI Workloads
entry.summary: Chiron: Cache Management Empowered by LLM Intelligence for AI Workloads arXiv · Nov 4, 2026AI clusters store data in remote object stores and use local caches so GPUs do not wait for data. This paper presents Chiron, a cache system in which a large language model asynchronously diagnoses access patterns and recommends a policy, while a deterministic harness reviews that advice, runs expert-designed policies locally, and returns cache feedback. Implemented on JuiceFS and evaluated on nine AI workloads, it reduces job completion time by 14.3-41.2% over the best baseline on popular AI workloads.

entry.title: AssameseLM-E2B: A small open-weight language model for Assamese that runs on consumer hardware
entry.summary: AssameseLM-E2B: An Open-Weight Assamese Language Model for Efficient Consumer-Grade Deployment arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces AssameseLM-E2B and its instruction-tuned version, AssameseLM-E2B-it, two 2-billion-parameter models adapted to the low-resource Assamese language. Built on the Gemma-4 architecture, the model uses an expanded byte-level BPE vocabulary and was trained with parameter-efficient continual pre-training and supervised fine-tuning. It reports a Bits-per-Byte score of 0.7488 on FLORES-200, a 96.7% overall RAG score, and 100% refusal accuracy on adversarial unanswerable prompts.

entry.title: Reasoning-aware unlearning of visual-to-knowledge links in multimodal reasoning models
entry.summary: Reasoning-Aware Cross-Modal Association Unlearning in Multimodal Large Reasoning Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how to remove the link between a visual input and sensitive knowledge in multimodal large reasoning models, so the model no longer exposes that information under the designated visual context. The authors propose Visual-Keyed Counterfactual Rebinding (VKCR), a parameter-efficient method that edits a compact association-conditioned parameter subspace and rebinds affected reasoning toward valid non-sensitive alternatives. They also introduce the CLEAR-R and MLLMU-R benchmarks to measure target leakage, hallucinated reassociation, and reasoning preservation. Experiments report substantially reduced image-conditioned target leakage and hallucinated reassociation while preserving non-sensitive visual reasoning and permitted text-only knowledge.

entry.title: FaCoDiff: A Diffusion Model for Forecasting Many Related Quantities Together
entry.summary: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes FaCoDiff, a method for multivariate probabilistic forecasting that models how variables depend on one another while controlling each variable's uncertainty. It uses history-conditioned factor loadings and structured denoising to avoid costly dense covariance computations. Across nine datasets, FaCoDiff achieves the lowest mean variogram score on eight of them.</summary>

entry.title: DSRS: Teaching Multimodal LLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes
entry.summary: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation (DSRS), a task requiring models to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect risks, and understand traffic rules to produce accurate segmentation masks. The authors build a benchmark dataset for the task and propose DSRS-Net, which adds geometric features without disrupting the original multimodal fusion mechanism. Experiments report that DSRS-Net performs better on driving scene reasoning segmentation and other language-driven segmentation tasks across public datasets.

entry.title: Regret bounds for market making with orders that stay active until filled
entry.summary: Regret Bounds for Market Making with Persistent Orders arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies adversarial market making where orders remain active until executed, with positions hedged on a secondary market. The authors give a simple deterministic policy with regret bounds against both a best fixed quote and a best quote per submission date. The rates remain optimal even when the exposure terms vanish, and lower bounds show those terms are necessary.

entry.title: Selective Prediction Intervals: a method that predicts, bounds, and abstains together
entry.summary: Selective Prediction Intervals: Jointly Learning to Predict, Bound, and Abstain arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces SelPI, which jointly trains interval, point-value, and abstention heads under one loss with an explicit acceptance-rate budget. It finds that interval width predicts large point errors but is anti-correlated with interval misses, so abstaining on wide intervals is a poor rule. Across 18 tabular benchmarks, the learned gate outperforms width thresholding and deep-ensemble disagreement selection on a proper interval score.

entry.title: Neural stochastic model for simulating lateral diffusion of membrane molecules
entry.summary: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a neural stochastic model that forecasts collective diffusion of membrane proteins from coarse-grained molecular dynamics trajectories. The model combines a transformer-based protein configuration encoder, multi-scale recurrent networks, and a stochastic latent process with learned memory, with a cross-attention decoder generating correlated displacements. Tested on seven PIEZO channels and a mixed PIEZO-TREK system, it reproduces the anomalous diffusion exponent of about 1 seen in MD and generates trajectories up to 40,000 frames.

entry.title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Super-Resolution Paper
entry.summary: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes CARM (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking), a statistical framework for adaptive spatial risk control under temporal distribution shift in scientific super-resolution. It converts spatial uncertainty scores into trust masks by online aggregation of threshold proposals from experts with different update rates. Experiments on a South China Sea chlorophyll-a daily stream, along with ERA5 wind and OSTIA sea-surface temperature data, show reduced empirical violation rates while retaining a non-trivial trusted region.

entry.title: Locating Video Moments Using Only Text Training
entry.summary: Grounding in the Dark: Text-Only Training for Zero-Shot Video Temporal Localization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether a text-only language model, without vision-language pretraining, can learn temporal grounding from textual video descriptions alone and receive video only at inference. The authors build a 134K-example text corpus and adapt Qwen3-8B with LoRA, evaluating on Charades-STA and QV-Highlights. To narrow the text-to-video modality gap, they propose Nearest Entity Replacement, a training-free method that reaches 14.45 and 20.72 mtIoU on the two benchmarks.

entry.title: PTQ4SAM3: A semantics-preserving method for compressing the SAM 3 segmentation model
entry.summary: PTQ4SAM3: Semantics-Preserving Post-Training Quantization for Segment Anything Model 3 arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) segments objects from text prompts and tracks them in video, but its memory and computation costs are high. The paper proposes Semantics-Preserving Quantization (SPQ), a post-training quantization method that weights concept-sensitive parameters more heavily, preserves residual features, and corrects mean error in video memory, all offline without adding inference operators. With a W4A8 image encoder, SPQ raises RefCOCO Pr@0.5 from 42.1 to 72.5 over PTQ4SAM while keeping 54.8 COCO mask AP.

entry.title: RDT-3D: Resolution-decoupled training for generating detailed 3D shapes
entry.summary: RDT-3D: Resolution-Decoupled Training for High-Fidelity 3D Geometry Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes Resolution-Decoupled Training (RDT), which anchors positional guidance at 512 resolution while supervising geometry at 1536 to reduce the mismatch between training and high-resolution inference. The authors also release Dual3D-300K, a dataset of 300K watertight 3D point clouds aligned across 512 and 1536 resolutions. Experiments show that RDT substantially improves sharp geometric regions.

entry.title: Speeding up long-context decoding in large hybrid LLMs without retraining
entry.summary: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper speeds up the remaining full-attention layers of hybrid large language models without any training or weight changes, using combined sparse attention over recent tokens, a pinned prefix, and a fixed budget of relevant context tokens. Per-layer window sizes and budgets are chosen with a multi-objective search. Across six models from three families, ranging from 4B to 397B parameters, the selected configurations keep baseline accuracy on 21 long-context datasets. Decoding 64k/256k tokens is up to 1.26x/2.22x faster on Qwen3.5-4B, 1.20x/2.23x on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, and 1.16x/2.06x on Ornith-1.0-397B.

entry.title: Growing One's Own AI Tools: Tools That Develop Through Practice
entry.summary: Growing One's AI Tools: A Paradigm of Practice-Grown Tools arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper reports how a conference interpreter with no programming training built and iteratively developed her own computer-assisted interpreting tool. Drawing on an eight-week version-controlled record, telemetry from 133 sessions, and over 20,000 recognized utterances, it traces how real conference work drove 62 commits and six versions. The author proposes a paradigm of practice-grown tools and formulates three propositions for assessing practitioners together with their tools.

entry.title: Short-term forecasts for many wind farms using one shared transformer model
entry.summary: Short-Term Forecasting of Heterogeneous Wind Power Fleets: Global Temporal Fusion Transformer Leveraging Static Covariates arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study tests a single global temporal fusion transformer trained jointly on many German wind farms, compared with separate local models and a linear baseline, for 48-hour-ahead power forecasting. It uses numerical weather prediction data and static farm characteristics such as altitude and hub height. The global model beat local models for 87% of synthetic and 77% of real wind farms, but only when static covariates were included.

entry.title: From handcrafted to generative: RLVR-optimized icon generation for Alexa+
entry.summary: From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+ arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Alexa+ screen devices display animated icons during conversations to visually reinforce spoken content. Previously these icons were hand-drawn one by one by designers, which was time-consuming and could not cover the wide range of topics in open-ended conversation. The paper describes an automated pipeline, already deployed in production, that generates vectorised animated icons from text descriptions alone. Its first stage, image generation, is the focus: the authors design objective verifiers that flag outputs violating design guidelines and use them to fine-tune a flow matching model via reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR), raising the pass rate from 15.7% to 58.7%.

entry.title: Distributed equivariant attention model for ab initio-accuracy molecular dynamics at tens-of-millions-of-atom scale
entry.summary: Ab Initio Accuracy Beyond the Cutoff: Distributed Message-Passing Equivariant Attention at Tens-of-Millions-of-Atom Scale arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents Tessera, a distributed runtime for equivariant message-passing Transformer models that learn ab initio-level potentials for molecular dynamics. It partitions atoms along a space-filling curve into equal-count shards, fixes tensor shapes between neighbor-list rebuilds, and uses CUDA Graph replay, fused kernels, and overlapped communication. Reported results include 30.7M atoms on 512 GPUs at 89.7% weak-scaling efficiency, and stable energy drift and structure in simulations of a 10.24M-atom salt solution and a 10.06M-atom Norovirus capsid.

entry.title: ReactWorld: Structured Interaction Responses for Robot-Driven Video Generation
entry.summary: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model that predicts how scenes change when a robot acts. It uses an interaction response field predictor to anticipate participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes, and a response feedback adapter to update object features and guide temporal attention across frames. The authors report an average score of 77.51 on RBench, 3.29 points above PhysisForcing, and a Domain score of 86.98 and average score of 81.87 on EZS-Bench.

entry.title: The Harness Is the Model: How Agent Scaffolding Affects a Fixed LLM's Banking Rule Compliance
entry.summary: The Harness Is the Model: Agent Scaffolding Changes a Fixed LLM's Compliance with Banking Conduct Rules, Unevenly Across Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper tests whether the agent harness around a fixed language model changes its compliance with banking conduct rules in a simulated retail bank. Four open-weight models were each run under five harnesses on 156 pre-registered cases covering EU consumer-credit, payments, investor-protection, data-protection and anti-money-laundering provisions. The harness effect varied strongly by model, a same-model reviewer reduced violations, and date-arithmetic rules failed in every harness. The authors argue validation should target model-harness pairs and check action logs rather than conversations.

entry.title: Cross-modal retrieval that handles both missing data types and noisy labels using semantic priors
entry.summary: Semantic Prior-Guided Incomplete Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes SPIRN, a framework for cross-modal retrieval that jointly addresses missing modalities and noisy labels. It uses fixed semantic priors as a stable reference for representation learning, noise handling, label calibration, and imputation of missing modalities. The authors state it is the first CMR framework to tackle both challenges together, and report that it outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods on four benchmark datasets.

entry.title: Mechanism-level benchmark and debate framework for detecting scam videos online
entry.summary: Beyond Risk Cues: A Mechanism-Level Benchmark and Verifiable Debate for Scam Video Detection on the Web arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces MechScam, a benchmark of 6,614 videos covering diverse scam mechanisms and non-scam categories, with video-supported explanations, annotations of potential scam elements, and misleading arguments built from genuine evidence. It also proposes ScamCourt, a debate framework in which trained prosecution and defense debaters argue opposing positions and a trained judge decides based on a transcript with verified citations. Experiments reportedly show that state-of-the-art MLLMs struggle to separate scam videos from similar non-scam content, while ScamCourt outperforms larger MLLMs and same-backbone fine-tuned baselines with fewer false positives.

entry.title: Deciding When to Verbalize Reasoning in Latent Thought Models
entry.summary: Learning When to Think Aloud in Latent Reasoning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces VITAL, a hybrid reasoning framework for language models that keeps most intermediate computation in hidden states while explicitly verbalizing only important tokens as reasoning anchors. A lightweight gating head chooses between explicit token generation and direct hidden-state feedback. Training combines curriculum-based supervised learning with reinforcement learning using a reward that balances correctness and conciseness. The authors report that VITAL outperforms fully latent reasoning methods at comparable reasoning lengths, and on Qwen3-1.7B achieves higher accuracy with shorter reasoning trajectories than hybrid baselines.

entry.title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Using Global and Local Semantic Consistency
entry.summary: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents XuanJian-DINOSAR, a foundation model for synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, trained through self-supervised learning on over 360K public SAR images. It adapts the optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR by combining global semantic self-distillation, local masked modeling, and feature-distribution regularization. A local consistency branch designed for SAR intensity statistics aligns features under Gamma speckle perturbations. The authors report state-of-the-art results on most metrics across multiple downstream classification and detection datasets.

entry.title: Many Pixels, One Composition: Self-Supervised Spectral Learning for Predicting Specimen Element Composition
entry.summary: Many Pixels, One Composition: Self-Supervised Spectra for Specimen-Level Prediction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper examines whether hyperspectral imaging can predict the elemental composition of physical specimens on Earth's surface. The authors train a pixel-level encoder self-supervised, then freeze it and train a lightweight attention-based regression head that pairs many representations of each specimen with its elemental label. On test specimens, the approach significantly outperforms traditional spectral matching and unmixing baselines, and outperforms supervised models based on the mean spectrum. Full model fine-tuning performs best but at substantially higher model capacity.

entry.title: Reasoning-Trace Overflow in Code Generation: A Study of Reasoning Models
entry.summary: Reasoning-Trace Overflow in Code Generation: An Empirical Study of Explicit Reasoning Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies a problem in small open-weight reasoning models, where the model spends so much of its output budget on reasoning that it never produces usable code. The authors test seven models across six code benchmark settings, measuring how much of a fixed 32k-token budget goes to reasoning and whether lightweight inference-time controls help. They find overflow is rare on simpler tasks but common on harder benchmarks and for certain model families.

entry.title: Drift-Adaptive Representation Preservation for Learning Across Changing Image Domains
entry.summary: Drift-adaptive Representation Preservation for Domain-Incremental Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper addresses forgetting in domain-incremental learning, where a pretrained vision model adapts to new input distributions and degrades on earlier domains. It tracks each past domain-class concept by its representation drift from a fixed anchor, using this drift as a surrogate for forgetting risk. High-drift concepts receive stronger preservation through a consolidation loss and less influence in prototype construction. The method repurposes a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to measure drift from compact stored context summaries rather than raw past data. Experiments on DomainNet, Office-Home, CORe50, and CDDB-Hard report a strong accuracy-forgetting balance with lower training memory and the smallest storage among compared methods.

entry.title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: a benchmark for checking scientific claims against paper tables and figures.
entry.summary: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper gives an overview of SciClaimEval, a pilot task at NTCIR-19 that asks systems to verify scientific claims against the tables and figures of the papers they come from. The dataset uses claims from 180 papers in machine learning, natural language processing, and medicine, paired with supporting evidence and a minimally modified non-supporting version. Twenty-two teams registered and 14 submitted 177 runs, mostly built on multimodal large language models. The best pair accuracy on the first subtask was 98.1%, but systems judging each claim-evidence pair separately scored 24.3 points lower.

entry.title: STARE: Scene text-aware multimodal retrieval for finding everyday objects by robots
entry.summary: STARE: Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies service robots that find and carry everyday objects based on free-form instructions that may mention visual features and scene text. The proposed STARE method combines visual and textual cues, uses a Crosslingual Visual Prompt to improve scene text interpretation, and models relationships between named entities in instructions and their objects. On two new benchmarks, STARE outperforms all baselines on standard multimodal retrieval metrics and reaches an 80% overall success rate in zero-shot physical experiments.

entry.title: GeoBiaset: A Benchmark Testing Whether Location Models Are Biased by Inserted People
entry.summary: GeoBiaset: A Counterfactual Benchmark for Demographic Bias in World-Level Geolocalization arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces GeoBiaset, the first benchmark for testing whether image geolocalization models are influenced by the apparent race of a person placed in the foreground. It contains 9,541 images created by inserting people of seven races into geotagged background photos while keeping the ground-truth coordinates unchanged. The authors also propose Person-Origin Perturbation Indicators (POPI) to measure whether predictions are pulled toward the region linked to the inserted group. Evaluations show continent-level performance drops of 16-47% when a demographically mismatched person is inserted.

entry.title: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories: A method to speed up hybrid language model inference by cutting memory and compute costs
entry.summary: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes SEED, a method that reduces the compute and memory cost of hybrid language models, which keep memories of earlier tokens in every layer. It generates deep-layer memories from a shallow anchor layer using trained write paths, so all prompt tokens except the last run through about 63% of the layers. It also stores each recurrent state as a rank-one sink plus low-rank factors. Across six checkpoints of five production hybrids, the method is nearly lossless on eleven official exams, and on NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with SGLang it raises Qwen3.8-Flash-Next per-GPU throughput by 1.2 to 1.4 times.

entry.title: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Tuning Using Library Performance Contracts
entry.summary: SysPilot: Cross-Library Performance Autotuning via Library Performance Contracts arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents SysPilot, an autotuning system that improves performance when several software libraries run together and compete for shared resources such as CPU cores, GPUs, and memory bandwidth. It describes each library with a Library Performance Contract, a specification of its resource demands, assumptions, controls, and observable signals, generated from documentation and code. SysPilot composes these contracts for an application, forms conflict hypotheses, validates them by profiling, and selects candidate configurations. On a benchmark suite of cross-library contention scenarios, it matches autotuners that need application-specific manual input, and it outperforms OpenTuner and SMAC3 by up to an additional 38% using 3x fewer runs.

entry.title: UniCompress: Merging Multiple Task Experts into One Compact Vision-Language Model for Edge Devices
entry.summary: UniCompress: From Multi-LoRA Experts to One Compact Model for Edge Intelligence arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents UniCompress, a framework that merges multiple task adapters into one compact, adapter-free vision-language model for embodied and edge devices. It starts from a BF16 Qwen3-VL-4B teacher and builds an asymmetric INT2 student using GPTQ initialization and teacher-guided quantization recovery, jointly compressing the vision encoder and language backbone. Evaluated on four embodied tasks, the model cuts weight storage from 8.9 GB to 2.1 GB, about 76% reduction. Its INT2 macro task score is 34.3 points above GPTQ-INT2 and within 0.9 points of the BF16 teacher.

entry.title: Which One Is Sounding? Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation
entry.summary: Which One Is Sounding? Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a method that uses binaural audio to identify which of several same-class visual candidates is actually producing sound in audio-visual segmentation. The approach grounds candidate regions with audio prompts, projects binaural cues onto a spatial response map, and refines the sounding instance's mask through spatial conditioning at both feature and decoder levels. Experiments on the binaurally extended AVS-Synthetic benchmark and the Habitat-AVS robotic indoor dataset show the best results on multi-candidate subsets, with reduced false activation on non-sounding regions.

entry.title: RouTex: Multi-Reference 3D Texture Generation via Rotary Position Encoding Reprogramming
entry.summary: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents RouTex, a framework for generating 3D textures conditioned on multiple reference images, built on in-context Diffusion Transformers. It reprograms the native 3D Rotary Position Encoding through Positional Routing to establish reference-to-view correspondence without adding parameters. Dual-Granularity Attention combines per-view local attention with global attention across deduplicated references. The authors report state-of-the-art results in multi-reference 3D texture generation.

entry.title: PRISM-AMC: A replay-free continual learning method for classifying radio modulation types
entry.summary: PRISM-AMC: Replay-Free Continual Learning for Automatic Modulation Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes PRISM-AMC, a replay-free continual learning framework for automatic modulation classification in wireless systems. It uses gradient projection memory to preserve task-relevant subspaces of intermediate representations, reducing catastrophic forgetting without storing raw I/Q samples. The method is evaluated in class-incremental and domain-incremental settings on the MIGOU and DeepSig 2018.01A datasets. It shows substantially less forgetting than sequential fine-tuning and elastic weight consolidation, and performs competitively with or better than replay-based RSD-AMC in class-incremental settings.

entry.title: ProcessPrefBench: Testing whether AI assistants apply a user's work-process preferences across tasks
entry.summary: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces ProcessPrefBench, a benchmark built from three months of natural dialogues between AI assistants and two knowledge workers. It contains 66 source-target case pairs to test whether a preference expressed in one conversation shapes a later answer on a task that does not restate it. Full-history and distilled-preference prompts improved preference realization over target-only prompting, but also increased fabricated-evidence failures. The authors highlight this trade-off between honoring user preferences and maintaining factual reliability.

entry.title: Learning from static context in federated time series forecasting
entry.summary: Learning From Static Context in Federated Time Series Forecasting arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies whether federated time series forecasting models, such as the Temporal Fusion Transformer, can learn from static inputs that describe each series when each client holds a single series. The authors compare federated optimization methods and find that per-batch FedAdam uses the static input nearly as well as central training, while communication-efficient methods with local epochs extract much less. Experiments use building energy, wind power, and synthetic datasets.

entry.title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: lower text loss did not mean better comprehension
entry.summary: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The authors trained small LoRA adapters on Tajik news and books, which lowered Qwen3's Tajik text loss at every model size from 0.6B to 8B. On the Belebele Tajik reading comprehension benchmark, however, most adapters did not improve accuracy, and one lowered it. At 8B, continued pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning produced a main model, e3, that scores higher on Belebele than Qwen3-8B; the paper also reports training problems encountered along the way.

entry.title: Touché World technical report: toward online unified camera and hand exploration in generative worlds
entry.summary: TouchéWorld tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Touché World, a framework that adds gesture-driven hand interaction to a camera-controlled video world model. Given an initial image and a scene description, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. The authors build joint camera-hand training data from egocentric videos and use causal adaptation and few-step distillation for chunk-level online generation. They also introduce the TouchéBench benchmark for evaluation.

entry.title: Improving deep graph-level clustering to avoid poor effectiveness and multi-class collapse
entry.summary: Alleviating Limited Effectiveness and Multi-Class Collapse in Deep Graph-level Clustering arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes S³GLC, a framework that groups graphs into semantically meaningful clusters by combining global topological features with local neighborhood features. It builds a spectral signature, derived via the Hoffman-Wielandt inequality, as a lower bound on graph edit distance, and fuses it with spatial representations through a sparse regression module. To reduce clustering collapse, it adds a balanced objective based on optimal transport using Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization. The authors report outperforming 15 baselines across 10 real-world datasets.

entry.title: Negative Weights in Reservoir Computing: How Link-Sign Ratios Affect Time-Series Forecasting
entry.summary: Impact of Negative Weights on Performance in Reservoir Computing arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study examines reservoir computing, where only the readout layer is trained while a fixed recurrent reservoir is used, focusing on how the share of negative links in a signed Erdos-Renyi reservoir affects an echo state network on the Mackey-Glass chaotic forecasting benchmark. The authors use two Shannon-entropy measures, node-state entropy and node-frequency entropy, to assess the diversity of reservoir states and temporal activation patterns. They report that intermediate negative sign ratios yield richer internal dynamics and much lower prediction error than all-positive or all-negative extremes. The authors caution that these findings are limited to the current benchmark and setting and need broader validation across other tasks, topologies, and spectral conditions.

entry.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent That Improves Itself
entry.summary: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Reglos, a training-free personal memory agent that updates each user's memory record after every conversation, with new preferences replacing old ones and facts able to be forgotten. Its harness is improved through recursive self-improvement, where a coding agent proposes patches from failure traces and a critic from a different model family screens them for benchmark gaming. With the same backbone across systems, Reglos outperforms memory systems such as Mem0, MemOS and EverOS on PersonaMem-v2 and LongMemEval-S.

entry.title: SVGFaith: Meta-Evaluating Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation
entry.summary: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces SVGFaith, a framework for testing whether metrics that judge how faithfully text-to-SVG systems follow prompts are reliable. It includes a controlled diagnostic set of 1,842 contrastive pairs across eight capability axes and a set of 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs. The authors also propose SVGFaith-Score, an interpretable pointwise metric that checks atomic visual requirements derived from each prompt, and report that it outperforms nine baselines.

entry.title: RI-Prune: Smarter Visual Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models Handling Multiple Images
entry.summary: RI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Vision-language models that process multiple images generate far more visual tokens, making pruning necessary. The authors find that existing attention-based pruning methods perform only marginally better than random selection in this setting. They propose RI-Prune, a training-free, attention-free method that scores tokens using query relevance, cross-image correspondence, and within-image representativeness, then selects tokens evenly across images. Across several benchmarks and three model backbones, RI-Prune gives a better balance between token reduction and task performance, especially under tight budgets.

entry.title: DeepfakeGenome: A benchmark for next-generation deepfake attribution
entry.summary: DeepfakeGenome: Toward Next-Generation Deepfake Attribution arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces DeepfakeGenome (DFG), a comprehensive benchmark for deepfake detection and attribution. It includes 100 facial forgery algorithms and 2M images, 4 to 100 times larger than prior attribution benchmarks. The authors design four evaluation protocols, including a retrieval-based attribution paradigm, and report over 2,000 experiments yielding 10 findings.

entry.title: Do search-augmented recommenders actually use the latest search?
entry.summary: Do Search-Augmented Recommenders Use the Latest Search Episode? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper introduces FocalSwap, an audit that replaces search inputs in recommendation models while holding the target, candidates, history, and scorer fixed, to test how much the latest search contributes. It compares neutral masks against category-matched observed search replacements on KuaiSAR and Qilin using SESRec and UniSAR checkpoints. Under the primary neutral-mask and category-matched controls, a positive contribution from the latest search slot is not established for SESRec or UniSAR.

entry.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A streaming speech recognition model whose earlier output never changes
entry.summary: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Confucius4-R2T2, a streaming speech recognition model that never revises the text it has already output. It is built by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on 1,500 hours of Chinese and English audio while freezing its pre-trained audio encoder and projector. The authors introduce the concept of Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) and use LSP-based labels to convert a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming model without architectural changes. The model weights and code are publicly released.

entry.title: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration via Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling
entry.summary: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration with Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents UniRestorer++, a framework that handles diverse image degradations within a single model and scales through multi-granularity degradation modeling. It progressively refines degradation groups, assigns group-specific experts, and uses routing to select a path and granularity level. The authors also introduce CDD-50, a benchmark covering 50 degradation categories, and report state-of-the-art results along with zero-shot generalization and few-shot transfer on real-world images.

entry.title: USI-Brain: Vision-language model for underwater spatial reasoning
entry.summary: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses underwater images, where scattering, color distortion, and low visibility obscure object boundaries and geometric cues needed for spatial reasoning. The authors build a spatial data engine combining enhancement, 2D and geometry-assisted question generation, and expert filtering, producing 4.27M QA pairs across five capability groups. They train USI-Brain with an Underwater Prior-guided Rectifier that applies gated corrections to visual features. On their USI-Bench, USI-Brain and USI-Brain + UPR improve over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct by 5.76 and 7.63 points on average across 15 task metrics.

entry.title: Act-HiMotif: A Hierarchical Model That Generates Daily Activity Schedules Using Reusable Activity-Structure Patterns
entry.summary: Act-HiMotif: Hierarchical Daily Activity Schedule Generation via Learned Activity-Structure Motifs arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents Act-HiMotif, a model that generates daily activity schedules from individual attributes such as age and income, for use in activity-based travel modeling and human behavior simulation. The model first separates home-only days from active days, then samples a reusable activity-structure motif from a profile-conditioned prior to guide schedule generation. A budget-constrained duration allocator then assigns activity durations that sum exactly to the full-day horizon. Experiments on large-scale travel survey data show it outperforms strong baselines in both in-distribution and spatial generalization settings.

entry.title: TRACK: Multiple-Instance Learning for Anti-Money Laundering in Transaction Networks
entry.summary: TRACK: Multiple Instance Learning for Anti-Money Laundering in Transaction Networks arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper points out that anti-money laundering investigations focus on accounts, yet suspicious evidence may appear in only a few transactions, and existing aggregation methods can mismatch this. The authors reformulate account-level detection as multiple instance learning and propose TRACK, which encodes each transaction with a shared encoder and selectively pools them into an account decision. Trained only on account-level labels, TRACK achieves the highest average precision among tabular and graph baselines on five datasets and ranks flagged transactions well above chance.

entry.title: Practical Estimation of the Best Possible Fairness-Accuracy Tradeoff Using Soft Labels
entry.summary: Practical Estimation of the Bayes Optimal Fairness-Accuracy Tradeoff with Soft Labels arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper studies the fundamental limit of the tradeoff between fairness and accuracy in classification. It derives an explicit expression for the fair Bayes error rate, the best achievable error under given fairness constraints. The authors build consistent estimators that use only soft labels and group information, and they bound their bias and sample complexity. Experiments show the method gives a robust, low-variance estimate of the optimal tradeoff curve, even when soft labels are noisy.

entry.title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models
entry.summary: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper uses choosing a number from 1 to 30 as a controlled case for studying how language models process preference across layers and tokens. Using perturbation probing, gradient attribution, and activation interventions on Qwen3-4B, the authors trace how an edit changing 17 to 15 continues to influence the second digit. The results show that later computation changes how local contributions affect the continuation, but the study does not establish the origin or full circuit of natural numerical preference.

entry.title: Attraction-ranking mismatch: theory and evidence from Hamiltonian feature dynamics for out-of-distribution detection
entry.summary: Attraction-Ranking Mismatch in Out-of-Distribution Detection: Theory and Evidence from Hamiltonian Feature Dynamics arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper asks whether pulling features toward learned in-distribution (ID) regions actually improves out-of-distribution (OOD) detection. Using class-conditioned Hamiltonian dynamics as a controlled testbed, the authors show that improving per-class affinity scores does not necessarily improve the ranking of ID versus OOD samples. An exact AUROC decomposition and local boundary analysis attribute first-order AUROC changes to relative score changes at the ID-OOD ranking boundary. Experiments show a score-aligned rule can improve a held-out source validation split yet consistently degrade performance after transfer.

entry.title: METRIC-GS: Selective Metric-Scale Estimation for 3D Gaussian Splatting
entry.summary: METRIC-GS: Selective Metric-Scale Estimation for 3D Gaussian Splatting arXiv · Nov 4, 20263D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions use arbitrary units from structure-from-motion, so they need a scale before they can be measured or used for AR content. METRIC-GS estimates scale for indoor photographs from the reconstruction's semantic content and abstains when evidence is thin, routing those cases to a heavier metric model. On 47 ScanNet++ scenes, the mean error drops from 21.1% to 16.6%, at about 11 seconds per scene.

entry.title: ChanSFormer: A Vision Transformer That Handles Any Image Channel Setup
entry.summary: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents ChanSFormer, a Vision Transformer designed to work with multi-channel images without depending on a fixed set of channels. It replaces rigid channel embeddings with disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens, keeping both channel identity and cross-channel information. On the JUMP-CP dataset it improves classification accuracy by 3.93% to 4.27% over state-of-the-art methods, and it reports 55% to 313% higher throughput.

entry.title: Training speech translation to preserve expressiveness using aligned parallel data
entry.summary: Holistic Parallel Supervision for Expressive Speech to Speech Translation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses the lack of expressiveness in speech-to-speech translation by building training data that aligns source and target speech in content, prosody, timing, and speaker identity, using professional dubbing and multilingual voice conversion. It also introduces DirectS2ST, an end-to-end method that predicts the full target speech representation directly from source speech. Experiments on English-German and English-Spanish show that this holistic parallel supervision improves expressive realization across evaluated systems, with DirectS2ST achieving the largest gains.

entry.title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predicting Motorcycle Movements in Crowded Traffic
entry.summary: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic arXiv · Nov 4, 2026MotoVerse is a benchmark for predictive perception from the viewpoint of a motorized two-wheeler rider in dense, unstructured traffic. It includes 949 maneuver clips and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 road agents, more than 16,000 of them two-wheelers. The benchmark covers two tasks, predicting the rider's maneuvers and forecasting the trajectories of other traffic agents. Experiments show that prediction errors are highest during left turns and under dynamic rider motion.

entry.title: Familiar letters, not related languages, bring unseen languages into a shared meaning space
entry.summary: Familiar letters, not related languages, let unseen languages into a shared space of meaning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents GlyphMind, a tokenizer-free vision transformer that reads text as pixels, pretrained to align translations across 27 writing systems. Adapted on untranslated Lao, it retrieved English translations seven times as often as the strongest simple baseline. Lao written in unfamiliar letters did not enter the shared space even though its close relative Thai was in pretraining, while Santali entered in the familiar Devanagari script but not in its own.

entry.title: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be?
entry.summary: How Unbalanced Must a Latin Rectangle Be? arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper treats a k×n Latin rectangle as n points in the grid [n]^k, calling it balanced when the points are pairwise equidistant in the ℓ1 metric, with imbalance measuring the distance from this ideal. It studies the minimum imbalance through simulated annealing, which improves 33 of 51 non-square reference values for 8≤n≤13, and a computer-assisted branch and bound that proves the minimum for a 3×9 rectangle is 56. It also gives Θ(n^3) asymptotics for fixed k, and all reported rectangles are checked in Lean 4.

entry.title: How Far Can Activation Steering Go? The Behavior-Capability Frontier in Contrastive Activation Addition
entry.summary: How Far Can You Steer? Behavior-Capability Frontiers in Contrastive Activation Addition arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA), a method that steers language model behavior by adding activation directions derived from contrasting examples. The authors select interventions that maximize behavioral gain under explicit limits on capability loss, evaluating four instruction-tuned models, seven behaviors, and capability-loss budgets of 1%, 3%, and 5%. Behavioral effects generalize strongly to held-out data, and the share of interventions preserving both behavior and capability rises sharply from 1% to 3% budgets, with little gain at 5%.

entry.title: Identifying which fine-tuned Stable Diffusion model made an image
entry.summary: Intra-Architecture Source Attribution for Stable Diffusion: A New Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces IntrAA-SD, a task for attributing a generated image to its source among Stable Diffusion models that share one architecture and differ only through fine-tuning. The authors release a benchmark of about 140K images generated from different fine-tunes of SDXL, using in-domain and out-of-distribution prompts. They also propose a baseline using a style-conditioned Mixture-of-Experts network, evaluated on attribution accuracy with ablation studies.

entry.title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
entry.summary: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes FedIA, a federated prompt learning framework that adapts vision-language models across decentralized clients without sharing raw data. It shifts personalization from the client level to the instance level, using global text prompts to select class-relevant image patches and generate instance-aware local text representations. An adaptive global-local fusion module then balances shared and local knowledge for each image-class pair. Experiments under domain shift and label skew settings report accuracy gains of 1.44% to 4.37% over the latest baseline.

entry.title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing via Multimodal Retrieval
entry.summary: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper introduces Clips2Story, a training-free pipeline that uses an LLM to build short videos from a pool of clips based on a user-specified keyword. It retrieves keyword-relevant clips using text descriptors, has the LLM arrange them into a storyboard with narrations, and retrieves visuals to match those narrations. Evaluated on a synthetic dataset built from 100 long-form videos, the method is reported to outperform a strong baseline in narrative coherence, keyword alignment, and realism in human evaluation.

entry.title: Controlled Experiments Comparing Configuration and Cache Design in LLM Serving Engines
entry.summary: A Controlled Experimental Evaluation of Configuration and Cache Architecture in LLM Serving Engines arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper compares vLLM and SGLang, two LLM serving engines, on multi-agent workloads that share prompt prefixes. The authors built a reproducible Kubernetes testbed and a seeded workload generator, then compared the engines under vendor defaults and with chunked prefill matched. Matching that one setting removes 78% of the capacity gap and 30 to 67% of the latency gap. At equal throughput, the remaining tail-latency advantage is 2.4 to 6.4x. The paper also offers six recommendations for comparing serving engines.

entry.title: A comparative study of how deep learning models over relational databases assign importance to columns
entry.summary: A Comparative Study of Importance Attribution to Columns in Deep Learning over Relational Databases arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper compares four methods for explaining deep learning models over relational databases by assigning importance scores to attributes: Monte Carlo Shapley, Kernel SHAP, single-attribute impact, and mask learning. It examines both the rankings of attributes and the distribution of their importance scores. Experiments on multiple datasets and two architectures show that methods agree more in regression than in classification. Single-attribute impact often yields explanations similar to Shapley-based methods at much lower computational cost.

entry.title: Study of Hyper-Connections design, proposing the simpler SimpleHC architecture
entry.summary: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper systematically studies the components of Hyper-Connections (HC), a residual architecture used in language models. It finds that learned read/write gating without mixing, and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates, each perform comparably to mHC, and identifies repeated access to the expanded residual state as a main source of training overhead. Based on these findings, it proposes SimpleHC, which removes residual mixing and shares memory access, adding only 2.4% training time over a vanilla residual baseline at the largest tested scale. The authors report that SimpleHC keeps performance comparable to mHC when scaling from 15B to 30B MoE models.

entry.title: PathoS2VD: Generating Pseudo Z-Stacks from 2D Pathology Slides
entry.summary: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes a generative framework that learns z-axis morphological priors from pathology z-stack data and transfers them to standard single-plane histopathology images. An image-to-video latent diffusion model synthesizes a pseudo z-stack from one 2D image, and a prior-preserving mixture fine-tuning strategy adapts it to new clinical datasets. The synthesized stacks show cross-plane morphological continuity and improve prostate cancer classification compared with conventional 2D representations.

entry.title: Ray-tracing-based dynamic channel sounding with autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI prediction
entry.summary: Ray-Tracing-Based Dynamic Channel Sounding With Autoregressive Wi-Fi CSI Prediction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper presents a dynamic channel sounding framework that combines autoregressive CSI prediction with SINR-constrained selection of sounding intervals. A Transformer with rotary position embedding predicts CSI across subcarriers from device positions for beamforming updates between sounding exchanges, evaluated with Sionna ray tracing. In single-STA Wi-Fi 7 link-level simulations, predicted-CSI beamforming improves mean goodput over stale CSI by 67.3%, 112.7%, and 119.1% for linear, circular, and cosine trajectories.

entry.title: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single-Image Reflection Removal
entry.summary: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses single-image reflection removal, which aims to recover the scene behind glass from a photo that also contains reflections. The authors propose CLEAR, a single-step, deterministic latent framework built on a pretrained latent diffusion model, with a physics-guided separator for transmission and reflection layers. A Hybrid Feature Alignment Module corrects high-frequency input features contaminated by reflection colors while keeping transmission-consistent texture. The authors report the best average fidelity and perceptual scores on six real-world benchmarks and the lowest LPIPS on every dataset.

entry.title: Robots in the City: A study of how urban robots shape pedestrians' perceived safety
entry.summary: Robots in the City: Persona-Based Perceptions of Urban Robots arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study examines whether robots in urban public spaces change how safe pedestrians feel on a street. The researchers created 18 images of Seoul streets varying in time of day, road class, and robot type (none, delivery robot, or humanoid). Two multimodal large language models, each conditioned on 500 synthetic personas, and 25 human respondents chose the safer image in each pair. Both models and humans preferred streets without robots and favored the delivery robot over the humanoid, with robots chosen more often at night.

entry.title: Graph-based LLM systems for agents: a survey
entry.summary: Graph-Mediated Large Language Model Systems in the Agentic Era: Reasoning, Knowledge, Retrieval, Execution, and Coordination arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This survey examines how graphs support large language model systems across reasoning, knowledge grounding, retrieval, memory, execution, and multi-agent coordination. It proposes an operation-level taxonomy that classifies each graph operation by its role and the component that computes it. The paper also presents an evaluation framework covering benchmarks, comparison designs, process diagnostics, and system costs, and identifies open challenges in adaptive computation, memory maintenance, and dependency-aware recovery.

entry.title: FLINT: Pairing Proximal Initialization with Bounded Noise for Flow-Matching Inverse Problems
entry.summary: FLINT: Coupling Proximal Initialization and Bounded Stochasticity for Flow-Matching Inverse Problems arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes FLINT, a two-stage framework for generative posterior sampling in imaging inverse problems using flow-matching models. It argues that trajectory-space methods and source-space methods, which optimize the initial noise, are coupled rather than independent, and derives a unified stability bound linking initialization proximity to cumulative sampling stochasticity. FLINT first obtains a high-fidelity starting point with a manifold-constrained proximal objective over a few iterations, then performs guided sampling under a bounded stochasticity schedule to preserve that initial advantage. Across diverse inverse problems, the authors report state-of-the-art perceptual quality, competitive distortion metrics, and superior computational efficiency.

entry.title: Reward budgeting to reduce early plateaus in RL for LLM reasoning
entry.summary: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper addresses early performance plateaus in reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning, which occur as the policy distribution becomes sharper. It introduces reward budgeting, which assigns a fixed total reward budget to each prompt to construct the advantage. Tested on Qwen3-8B and Llama3.2-3B-Instruct, the method improves several RL baselines, with gains up to +12.50 on AMC23 and +10.00 on AIME24 and AIME25.

entry.title: BAM: Bivariate Additive Models for Readable Tabular Prediction
entry.summary: BAM: Bivariate Additive Models for Interpretable Tabular Prediction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes Bivariate Additive Models (BAMs), a type of GA²M in which each pairwise shape function is limited to a simple parametric form, an asymmetric bivariate Gaussian. Each component can be shown as a single-peaked contour map, and its feature pair is chosen automatically during training. Experiments on six tabular benchmarks show that BAM's predictive accuracy is comparable to standard GAMs and close to GA²Ms. The paper also examines the trade-off between accuracy and the number of components a user must inspect.

entry.title: Combining Deep and Classical Methods: A CPU-Efficient Decision-Fusion Model for Modulation Recognition
entry.summary: Deep Meets Classical: A CPU-Efficient Decision-Fusion Model for Automatic Modulation Classification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses automatic modulation classification, identifying the modulation type of radio signals without cooperation. The authors find that a compact CNN on raw I/Q samples is more robust at low SNR, while a higher-order cumulant classifier is more accurate at high SNR. They propose FuseAMC, which fuses the two models' class posteriors with a logistic-regression combiner. On RadioML 2016.10a it reaches 55.8% overall accuracy and runs on a single CPU core.

entry.title: Diversity-aware replay sampling using statistical leverage scores
entry.summary: Diversity-Aware Experience Replay via Statistical Leverage Scores arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses reinforcement learning replay buffers that are dominated by routine transitions, so rare situations are seldom sampled. It scores each stored transition by its statistical leverage relative to the buffer's own data and mixes this score with uniform sampling. The authors find that importance-weight correction cancels the benefit, so they omit it, and they extend the approach to relational rare situations via goal-relative trajectory windows. On a three-joint arm pushing an object around an obstacle, rare-task success rises from 0.49 to 0.69.

entry.title: Modality-aware pruning of expert parameters in MoE multimodal language models
entry.summary: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper proposes MAEP, a training-free method for pruning experts in mixture-of-experts multimodal large language models. It scores expert importance separately for vision and text tokens in a single forward pass and ranks experts globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs show it beats modality-agnostic baselines on most multimodal benchmarks and stays competitive on text-only tasks, cutting BF16 expert weights by about 27 GB.

entry.title: Split-KV: Efficient Context Parallelism for Training Diffusion Drafters
entry.summary: Split-KV: Efficient Context Parallelism for Training Diffusion Drafters arXiv · Nov 4, 2026Diffusion drafters speed up speculative decoding by denoising several draft tokens in parallel, and their training uses short draft queries cross-attending to a much longer context. This paper presents Split-KV, an exact context parallelism method that keeps key/value shards local so per-layer communication scales with query size rather than context length. It adds a cost-aware longest-processing-time-first strategy to balance context chunks by their realized attention cost. At a context parallel size of 64, the authors report 85–91% weak-scaling efficiency and up to 3.67× speedup over the fastest existing baseline.

entry.title: 3D Banff Glomerulitis Scoring for Kidney Transplant Biopsies: Volumetric Quantification Feasibility Study
entry.summary: 3D Banff Glomerulitis Scoring for Kidney Transplant Pathology: Feasibility Study for Volumetric Quantification arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This study examines whether Banff glomerulitis scoring for kidney transplant biopsies can be extended from two to three dimensions. The authors propose a framework that aligns serial sections, tracks glomeruli across depth, and integrates inflammatory cell counts under three scoring strategies. Applied to multi-section renal allograft biopsies, the 3D g-scores were more consistent across sections. Under the semi-automatic setting, the Volumetric strategy correlated more strongly with clinical biomarkers than traditional 2D scores.

entry.title: Automated data pipelines for merging two Salesforce organizations after an acquisition
entry.summary: Autonomous ETL Pipelines for Salesforce M&A Consolidation: A Reference Framework, Jitterbit Mapping, and Reproducible Simulation Study arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a reference framework for an autonomous ETL pipeline that consolidates customer data from two Salesforce organizations while both remain in use. It covers bulk extraction, declarative mapping, quality gates, master data matching, constrained loading, and change data capture with a circuit breaker, each mapped to Jitterbit Integration Studio. Evaluated on synthetic scenarios with known ground truth, the hybrid matching reached pairwise F1 scores of 0.918 for accounts and 0.885 for contacts. Validation on a production deployment is left for future work.
